Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/tugging hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons and or resulting in bodily disability of a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
Point b What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-worth, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Point c What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her inner needs, forcing sexual relations, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction.
Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual relations committed against a person residing within the scope of the household, forced sexual relations against someone within the scope of one's household with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
Point d What is meant by "Economic Neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife and children or family or relatives such as not providing for the wife or spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers including acts of limiting or prohibiting family members from doing decent work.
Point e What is meant by "Restriction of movement" is limiting the movement of the wife or children to develop their potential whether for economic purposes or social purposes such as prohibiting gathering or socializing with the community as well as limiting relatives' space/movement such as preventing domestic workers and drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency.
6. Discrimination is any differentiation, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in the reduction, distortion, or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, such as parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, husbands, wives, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom (local wisdom) is truth that has become traditional or established in an area, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values.

1.9.rationale: In the Indonesian text (Penjelasan Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf c), the regulation defines “kekerasan seksual” to include “pemaksaan hubungan seksual … dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial dan/atau tujuan tertentu.” This is describing forced sexual acts (including coercing someone to have sex with another person for commercial purposes), i.e., sexual violence/sexual exploitation. However, the indicator is specifically “sexual slavery/exploitation.” The cited clause does not establish slavery-like conditions (ownership/control as property, forced labor/servitude), and the regulation does not explicitly mention “perbudakan seksual” (sexual slavery). The judge over-extended the definition of sexual violence into “sexual slavery-type conduct,” producing a false positive given the narrower indicator.

2.3.evaluator_rationale: The provided sentences discuss monitoring, evaluation, and annual reporting on implementation of minimum service standards, but they do not explicitly establish or assign responsibility for a system/entity to collect, record, manage, compile, exchange, or maintain data on violence cases or victims.

NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) developing the intellectual life of the nation and (4) participating in the implementation of world order based on (a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

Various acts of violence both against women and children inside the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Pakpak Bharat Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is the obligation of Regional Government as regulated in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government which states that: "in carrying out regional autonomy has the obligation to protect the community, maintain unity, integrity and national harmony as well as the integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia."

Based on that, the Government of Pakpak Bharat Regency has taken steps as efforts to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence, however it has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community especially to women and children due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, implementation has not been sustainable and so forth. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the protection of women and children from acts of violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence that occur.

With the enactment of this Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, in Pakpak Bharat Regency in particular, then handling, rehabilitation and reintegration can be carried out properly and more smoothly in the process of prevention and handling of violence against women and children which in its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, the community and also the participation of the business world in the prevention of violence against women and children from the beloved Pakpak Bharat Regency.

CHAPTER XIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 20
In the event that the PPT as referred to in Article 11 has not yet been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the tasks and functions of integrated services for women and children victims of violence in the region.

2.3.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation does not clearly establish a case/victim data collection system. The closest language is Pasal 9 ayat (2) huruf e: “membangun dan menyediakan sistem informasi yang lengkap dan mudah diakses,” but this is framed as a general prevention effort and does not specify collecting/recording/maintaining case data on violence, nor assign an entity to manage such data. Pasal 14–16 cover monitoring/evaluation and annual reporting of SPM implementation, not a data management system for cases. Therefore the judge’s “No” is consistent with the Indonesian text; the golden label “Yes” appears incorrect (or at least too generous for this indicator).

2.5.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences mention guidance, supervision, implementation instructions, and monitoring/evaluation, but they do not require or provide training, technical capacity building, or professional development for implementers or service providers.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency.
6. Discrimination is any differentiation, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in the reduction, distortion, or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, such as parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, husbands, wives, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom (local wisdom) is truth that has become traditional or established in an area, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values.

Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila) Letter b The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Governments to fulfill the rights of women and children victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e The principle of legal certainty is the best interest for women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo the sanction imposed upon them, or how children will face perpetrators in court proceedings, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.
Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who incidentally is a person they once loved, and so forth. So we as a society or as law enforcement officials need to give opportunities to children and women to express their interests concerning everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

CHAPTER X
FUNDING
Article 17
Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence, is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 18
(1) The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence in the Region.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes providing implementation instructions, guidance, supervision, monitoring and evaluation of service implementation for women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 14
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

NUMBER 2 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The national objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, as stipulated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution in the fourth paragraph are stated to include: (1) protecting the entire Indonesian nation and all Indonesian territory, (2) advancing public welfare, (3) developing the intellectual life of the nation and (4) participating in the implementation of world order based on (a) independence, (b) lasting peace, and (c) social justice.

The Republic of Indonesia is a State of Law (rechtstaat) and not a state of power (machstaat), so that all actions of its citizens, including those in the form of violence, committed by both men and women, are also regulated by law.

The rights of women and children are recognized as Human Rights (HAM), which must be upheld and respected by all parties, however in reality there are still many women and children who become victims of violence. The commitment of the Central Government to protect children and women is reflected in the legislation below it.

6.2.rationale: The Indonesian regulation includes trafficking in scope (Pasal 3(1) huruf a: “termasuk perdagangan orang”) and defines “perdagangan orang” (Pasal 1 angka 7). However, the indicator is specifically “Women victims of trafficking” as an intersectional group. The text treats trafficking generally (applies to “perempuan dan anak” broadly) and does not provide specific, tailored provisions for women trafficking victims as a distinct subgroup (e.g., special procedures/services for trafficking survivors). The judge inferred inclusion of women trafficking victims merely from mentioning trafficking and defining it, which is too lenient for an intersectional-indicator framing, producing a false positive.

6.8.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes services for reporters and witnesses and provides legal assistance and assistance by social workers/legal aid during examination processes, indicating coverage of women involved in legal processes (at least as witnesses/reporters/victims).

Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constitutes respect for human rights and the dignity of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (second principle of Pancasila) Letter b The principle of gender equality and justice, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of protection of victims' rights, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Governments to fulfill the rights of women and children victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e The principle of legal certainty is the best interest for women and children, constitutes a principle specific to women and children themselves such as for example, how the interests of child victims of violence to undergo the sanction imposed upon them, or how children will face perpetrators in court proceedings, must be stated in accordance with the interests of child victims of violence.
Likewise for women victims of violence who wish to be given freedom in accordance with their interests, women who wish to forget the perpetrator who incidentally is a person they once loved, and so forth. So we as a society or as law enforcement officials need to give opportunities to children and women to express their interests concerning everything related to the perpetrator as well as how to overcome the impact of violence that befalls them.

CHAPTER X
FUNDING
Article 17
Funding for the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence, is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. Other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pakpak Bharat Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Pakpak Bharat.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Social Service is the Social Service of Pakpak Bharat Regency.
6. Discrimination is any differentiation, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, resulting in the reduction, distortion, or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including those in the womb.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any action that results in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, such as parents, close family, teachers and companions.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the victim's condition including physical, psychological, and sexual health so that the victim can perform their role again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
14. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions normally.
15. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from a regional area to their area of origin.
16. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the regional government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
21. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children and mother and her children.
24. Household is family members and relatives such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, husbands, wives, cousins and so on and non-relatives such as domestic workers, drivers and so on who live and reside in one house.
25. Local wisdom (local wisdom) is truth that has become traditional or established in an area, local wisdom is a combination of sacred religious values and various existing values.

CHAPTER XIII
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 20
In the event that the PPT as referred to in Article 11 has not yet been established, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out the tasks and functions of integrated services for women and children victims of violence in the region.

Article 15
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or, if necessary, as needed.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 14
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.
(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus units that implement policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(4) Monitoring shall be conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, serious injury such as slapping, hitting, spitting on, pulling hair/tugging hair, kicking, burning with hot objects, hitting/injuring with weapons and or resulting in bodily disability of a person, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death.
Point b What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person. Psychological violence can take the form of emotional abuse, hurtful comments that even demean self-worth, isolating the wife from the outside world, threatening/intimidating as a means of imposing one's will.
Point c What is meant by "sexual violence" is violence against sexuality which includes isolating (distancing) the wife from her inner needs, forcing sexual relations, forcing one's own sexual preferences or not paying attention to the wife's satisfaction.
Sexual violence can also take the form of forced sexual relations committed against a person residing within the scope of the household, forced sexual relations against someone within the scope of one's household with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
Point d What is meant by "Economic Neglect" is neglecting the economic needs of the wife and children or family or relatives such as not providing for the wife or spending the wife's money, not giving or withholding the wages of domestic workers or drivers including acts of limiting or prohibiting family members from doing decent work.
Point e What is meant by "Restriction of movement" is limiting the movement of the wife or children to develop their potential whether for economic purposes or social purposes such as prohibiting gathering or socializing with the community as well as limiting relatives' space/movement such as preventing domestic workers and drivers from communicating or having contact with their families.

6.8.rationale: The Indonesian text provides services to “pelapor dan saksi” (Pasal 3(1) huruf d) and grants victims rights to assistance by social workers and legal aid “pada setiap tingkat proses pemeriksaan” (Pasal 4 huruf e). It also includes “bantuan hukum” as a PPT service (Pasal 11(4) huruf d). But the indicator is “Women in legal process” as an intersectional category (women involved in legal proceedings). The regulation does not single out women in legal processes as a distinct group needing tailored measures; it addresses victims (women/children) and also reporters/witnesses generally. The judge over-generalized these general legal-aid provisions into satisfying an intersectional indicator, leading to a false positive.
